correctness.rationale: Kaneko–Stoll Theorem 2.2 gives the strict global cutoff ab<2^23 for odd positive factors whose two binary weights and product weight are all three. Unique binary expansion gives precisely 231 candidate odd three-bit products 1+2^i+2^j (1<=i<j<=22). Trial division up to integer square root exhausts unordered factor pairs, yielding precisely six. Standalone verify.py replayed: 231 products, 5473 eligible trial divisors, and independent 3672 factor-first admissible pairs, both yielding exactly (7,7,49),(7,19,133),(7,37,259),(11,35,385),(13,21,273),(21,49,1029). All integer identities checked. The published cutoff, not finite computation alone, proves global completeness.

originality.rationale: The motivating published theorem supplies a general effective upper bound but not this sharp exact symmetric weight-three classification. The highly relevant published (3,2,3) finding addresses a disjoint factor-weight condition, as confirmed by reading its full RESULT.md. OEIS A080025 records the six product values as prior data, but its finite table terminates below the applicable 8,388,608 bound and does not imply global completeness for these six pairs. The specific original scope is the worldwide exact completeness and sharp maximum 1029, not discovery of these six values. Residual implicit-prior-coverage risk remains.
residual_risks: An unindexed earlier article, sequence commentary, or computation might give the same complete symmetric (3,3,3) classification.
The contribution is a narrow exact finite classification and sharp natural bound, based on a published deep theorem and substantial but elementary enumeration.

value.rationale: The symmetric first nonexceptional sparse binary-product case is a natural specific slice of Kaneko–Stoll’s Diophantine factor-weight question. It has six distinct unordered solutions, gives every factorization and improves the published effective ceiling ab<8,388,608 to an exact sharp maximum 1029. The exact finite cutoff globally excludes unobserved products. The answer is narrow and individual numerical products were known, but the complete rigorous solution of this naturally motivated symmetric case is not a routine mere parameter substitution or table listing.
